title: TaskSpec
description: Canonical (enriched) provider-neutral task contract for PromptForge Local. This is NOT what the model outputs: the compiler model targets schemas/compiler-output.schema.json, and the client enriches validated output with task_id, project_id and schema_version before validating against THIS schema. Only canonical TaskSpecs are rendered, stored, or exported. Mirrored 1:1 by the runtime Zod schema. See docs/TASKSPEC.md for field semantics and the full lifecycle.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Client-owned: stamped during enrichment. Required in canonical TaskSpecs; must be absent from compiler output.

task_id.description: Stable task identifier, e.g. TASK-2026-0042. Client-owned: assigned during enrichment; never produced by the compiler model (rejected at the compiler-output stage). Required in canonical TaskSpecs.

project_id.description: Identifier of the project this task belongs to. Client-owned: assigned during enrichment from the active project; never produced by the compiler model. Tasks never cross project boundaries. Required in canonical TaskSpecs.

task_type.description: Classification of the requested work. Drives context-selection heuristics.

execution_mode.description: Resolved depth of this compilation. The UI-level 'auto' value must be resolved to one of these before compilation; it never appears in a TaskSpec.

target_model.description: The AI model that will execute the task (e.g. 'deepseek-v4-pro', 'qwen-3.8-max', 'gpt-5.6-sol', 'opus-5'). This is the model identity, not the coding runtime.

agent_runtime.description: The coding agent/runtime that will execute the task. Determines which instruction file(s) and renderer family to use. AGENTS.md is shared across all runtimes; runtime-specific instruction files (QWEN.md, CLAUDE.md) are separate.

execution_profile.description: Declarative profile key (e.g. 'deepseek-v4-pro-claude-code') that adapts working style only. Profiles control planning depth, exploration budget, context reuse, reasoning effort, test strategy, retry budget, progress verbosity, autonomy and guardrail strength. The task meaning is identical across all profiles.

objective.description: One explicit sentence describing the outcome the coding agent must achieve.

user_value.description: Why this task matters to the user or product. Optional but encouraged.

current_state.description: Known facts about the project's current state that are material to this task. Facts only, no assumptions.

relevant_context.description: Repository-relative file paths the agent should read before starting (typically .promptforge/context/*.md files). Must only reference context actually supplied with the task.

assumptions.description: Decisions the compiler made without asking, each phrased so the user can veto it. Surfaced verbatim in the rendered prompt.

blocking_questions.description: At most three questions that block correct execution. Only for unknowns listed in the product spec's 'must ask' policy (billing provider, data deletion/migration, architecture-changing choices, authorization rules, ambiguous user intent).

scope.description: Concrete, bounded work items the agent must implement.

out_of_scope.description: Explicit exclusions that prevent scope expansion.

requirements.description: Category-grouped requirements. The client pre-fills missing categories with empty arrays before validation. Empty categories are normal and preferred over invented content.

edge_cases.description: Failure states and boundary conditions the implementation must handle.

execution_plan.description: Ordered implementation steps. Mandatory in spirit for 'deep' and 'plan' modes; optional for quick/standard.

test_plan.description: Targeted tests and validation commands the agent should run.

stop_conditions.description: Situations in which the agent must stop and ask instead of proceeding (destructive migrations, production deploys, irreversible operations).

final_report.description: Reporting requirements: items the executing agent must include in its completion report (e.g. changed files, test results, assumptions, remaining risks).

confidence.description: Model self-assessment of specification completeness. Informational only: never rendered as a quality score, only used to flag uncertainty in the checklist.

estimated_prompt_tokens.description: Model's own estimate of the rendered prompt size. Advisory only: the client recomputes the estimate locally and stores both values.
